bib.title: Automated flower classification over a large number of classes
bib.venue: ICVGIP 2008 (Indian Conference on Computer Vision, Graphics and Image Processing)

question: To what extent can combining several hand-designed features in a multiple-kernel SVM improve classification over a large number of visually similar flower classes?
hypothesis: Learning a per-class optimal weighting of colour, shape, texture and spatial-layout kernels will beat any single feature on a dataset with high between-class similarity.
contributions: Four flower-specific features (internal SIFT, boundary SIFT, HOG, HSV) combined with per-class multiple-kernel learning
New best result on the 17-class flower dataset (88.33%)

method.summary: Flowers are segmented from background with an iterative graph-cut and petal-shape-model scheme; four bag-of-visual-words features (HSV colour, foreground SIFT, boundary SIFT, HOG) are turned into chi-squared exponential kernels and combined with per-class weights learnt by Varma and Ray's convex MKL inside a one-vs-rest SVM. Vocabulary sizes and SIFT radius/spacing are tuned on a validation set, then the classifier is retrained on train+val.

datasets.name: 103-class flower dataset (later released as Oxford Flowers)
datasets.size: 8189 images, 103 classes, 40 to 250 images per class
datasets.source: Mostly web-collected, a few photographed by authors; flowers common in the UK; licence not stated
datasets.preprocessing: Images rescaled so smallest dimension is 500 px

datasets.name: 17-class flower dataset (Nilsback and Zisserman 2006)
datasets.split: not stated here; results are mean +- std, so presumably repeated splits (inferred: from the +- values)

models.name: Multiple-kernel SVM, one-vs-rest, kernels sum_f beta_f exp(-mu_f chi2_f)
models.architecture: SVM with weighted sum of chi-squared kernels; beta learnt per class by Varma and Ray [16]
models.vocab: visual words: colour 1000, internal SIFT 8000, boundary SIFT 3000, HOG 1500

other.mu_f: 1/mean chi2 distance between vectors over all training images
other.SIFT: 128-d, grey value only, rotation invariant, descriptors with L2 norm below 200 zeroed
other.prediction: classifier with most positive response over all classes

models.name: Nearest neighbour with chi2 distance (Nilsback and Zisserman 2006 features)
Varma and Ray MKL on 2006 features

training.objective: one-vs-rest SVM with learnt kernel weights (convex optimisation of Varma and Ray)

other.hyperparameter search: words 1000-10000 (colour 100-5000), R and M 5-50 px, each variable maximised separately on validation set
other.final fit: retrain on all training data (train plus val, 1030 each) after fixing parameters

metrics.name: mean per-class recognition rate
metrics.definition: classification accuracy averaged over classes, not over images (as Caltech101/256)

limits: 103-class test number is a single split (10 train/10 val per class) with no variance or seed reporting
Dataset has 103 classes in this paper; the later public Flowers-102 release differs in class count
Authors concede large within-class variation and few samples per class are the principal challenge
Boundary SIFT is sensitive to segmentation quality; pipeline depends on flower segmentation
SVM C, k-means init and compute are not stated; hand-crafted features, long superseded by deep features
